newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans 2.8trln rbl loan tender for gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans 2.8trln rbl loan tender for gold mine.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry will set up a tender with commercial banks which will allow it to borrow 2.8 trillion roubles on February 17 to finance gold mining, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday.
The government will start repaying the loan, which will be used to help pay off 1996 debts owed by the government to gold miners, in September or October, Livshits told a news conference.

"All the funds will be channelled to gold mining, bearing in mind that gold miners must receive them by the end of February," he said. "They are not enough to normalise the situation, but the sum is significant (enough) to relieve the situation."

A Russian Industry Ministry report in December last year said 1996 gold production was likely to fall to around 110 tonnes against 122 tonnes in 1995. It could fall sharply again in 1997, officials have said.
Producers have blamed the expected drop in 1997 output on the absence of a viable precious metals market and exchange.
Livshits said he favoured a slow transition to a precious metals market.
"My attitude is positive on the whole," he said. "We must develop the market, but slowly, bearing in mind guarantees of gold production. There must be an improvement, but it must happen slowly."
